about: Lessons from lunar landing attempts whose operators published a cause, each turned into an optional checklist item a project can adopt into its readiness list. The wording of each checklist item is this project's; the facts behind it are the source's.

records.name: Sensor safety interlocks set for flight
records.text: IM-1's laser rangefinders could not be used because their safety-enable switch was not changed before launch; only a NASA payload saved the descent.
records.checklist_item: Every landing sensor's safety interlock checked in its flight setting before the lander is closed out for launch.

sources.title: Simple Error Could Have Resulted in Intuitive Machines Mission Failure (Marc Boucher, 25 February 2024)

records.name: Altimeters and camera navigation tested in polar light
records.text: IM-2 hit the surface too fast after its altimeters gave noisy readings and long shadows from the low Sun confused its camera navigation.
records.checklist_item: Descent altimeters and camera navigation tested against low-Sun, long-shadow terrain like the landing site, with a different kind of altimeter as a backup.

sources.title: IM-2's Imperfect Landing Due to Altimeter Interference, South Pole Lighting Conditions

records.name: Altitude filter flown over the real approach terrain
records.text: HAKUTO-R Mission 1's software treated true altimeter readings as faulty after passing a crater rim about 3 km high, and ran out of propellant above the surface.
records.checklist_item: Navigation software run in simulation over the real terrain of the planned approach, including crater rims and cliffs.

sources.title: ispace Announces Results of the HAKUTO-R Mission 1 Lunar Landing (26 May 2023)

records.name: Rangefinder checked in flight before descent
records.text: HAKUTO-R Mission 2's laser rangefinder gave its first valid reading below about 900 m instead of about 3 km, so braking came too late; its performance had degraded in flight.
records.checklist_item: Laser rangefinder performance checked in flight before descent, with a plan for a late first reading.

sources.title: ispace Releases Technical Cause Analysis for HAKUTO-R Mission 2 (24 June 2025)

records.name: Descent guidance tested with a main engine lost
records.text: SLIM most likely lost the thrust of one of its two main engines at about 50 m altitude and still reached the surface 55 m from its target.
records.checklist_item: Descent guidance tested with one main engine lost at low altitude.

sources.title: Outcome for the Smart Lander for Investigating Moon (SLIM)'s Moon Landing (25 January 2024)

records.name: Pressure valves leak-checked after vibration
records.text: Peregrine lost its landing when helium pressure control valve PCV2 failed to seal, most likely from vibration-initiated relaxation between threaded parts inside the valve.
records.checklist_item: Propulsion pressure control valves leak-checked after vibration testing.
